items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: I was with Basie’s first band in 1932 or 33... I worked with him there in that band... Basie was the one that took over the band, then he sent and got me to join him again. So and that’s when I went back and worked with him I guess about 12 or 13 years off and on.

ctx.x: Now talk to us about when you first started with Basie.

Well I was with Basie’s first band in 1932 or 33, which was short-lived, and actually he was working with Benny Moten at that time. But Moten was having a lot of problems with getting work. So Basie got a job in I think it was Little Rock, Arkansas. And he came to Little Rock and I was there, and I worked with him there in that band.
How did you meet? How did you audition for him or get that spot?

items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: That's when I first met Basie. He was with the Blue Devils, Walter Page's Blue Devils.

ctx.x: Pigmeat Markham. I know he remembers him very well, because I've asked him, you know, like in later years, if they knew Bruce -- his name was Bruson or Bruce. And I remember him having a nice little sounding band, couldn't have been anymore than eight. But then -- but I don't know if that was the first or not, because I -- you know, as I said, I was listening to other bands like Alphonso Trent.
